findings.issue_text: [BUG] The public group members page now fetches members through findMembers(), which sends the model's default limit of 50, while the members.hbs template received no pagination controls, so members 51+ are unreachable. Any user browsing /groups/<name>/members of a group with more than 50 members sees a silently truncated list with no indication and no way to page; before this diff the backend returned all members of non-automatic groups (and up to 200 for automatic ones), so large groups (e.g. trust_level groups) lose most of their member list with no workaround in the UI.

[BUG] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overstates the page count by one whenever limit divides user_count exactly (ceil is required). For a group with exactly 50 or 100 members the admin page shows totalPages of 2/3 and showingLast is false on the real last page, so clicking next (whose clamp Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) at line 33 and findMembers' own Math.min(user_count, offset) clamp both permit offset == user_count) navigates to a page with zero members displayed as 'N/N'; the same empty page appears after removing a member when the count lands on a multiple of the page size.

[BUG] update assigns group.visible = (params[:visible] == "true") unconditionally, with no presence guard like the one alias_level gets, and the parameter moved from the old nested group[visible] form to a flat param. Any request that omits the flat visible param silently hides the group and still returns success_json: old-format API clients or scripts (still sending group[name]/group[visible], or legacy PATCH incremental changes:{add:...} requests, which this action now also handles) get name/alias_level ignored and visible flipped to false, so groups disappear from the site as a side effect of an unrelated save with no error reported.

[BUG] add_members calls group.add(user) for every CSV username with no check that the user is already a member, and the client never clears the add-members input after a successful add (the author's own TODO), so re-submitting an existing member inserts a second group_users join row. An admin who clicks the Add button again (the stale username is still in the input) or who types the name of someone already in the group creates a duplicate membership: the user appears twice in the member list, user_count is inflated (group.users.count counts join rows), and cleanup requires manual DB deletion; there is no unique index on group_users to raise an error.

[ADVISORY] The public GET /groups/:id/members response changed from a bare JSON array of users to an object of the form {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no compatibility path or consumer notification. Out-of-tree consumers of the endpoint (plugins, API scripts parsing the array) break silently after deploy; the diff updates the two in-repo consumers but nothing in the change surfaces the breakage to external users of the endpoint.

[ADVISORY] limit is taken verbatim from params with no upper bound ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i). Anyone who can see the group can request ?limit=999999 and dump the entire membership (and trigger the corresponding query/serialization load) in a single request; the old code at least capped automatic-group listings at 200, so this diff removes the only bound the endpoint had.

[ADVISORY] The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" spec exercises remove_member with xhr :put while the route added in this diff (delete "members" => "groups#remove_member") and the client model both use DELETE. The spec passes regardless of the route's HTTP verb (controller specs bypass routing), so a verb typo or routes.rb regression on the new DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoint ships undetected; the sibling add_members spec at least matches its PUT route.

[ADVISORY] Neither removeMember nor addMembers attaches a rejection handler to the ajax promise, and the controller actions that invoke them (admin-group.js.es6 removeMember/addMembers) also swallow rejections. When the DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/<id>/members.json call fails (expired admin session returning 403, CSRF token mismatch, or a 422), the bootbox confirm closes, the member list never reloads, and no error is shown: the admin repeats the remove/add with zero feedback and no console-visible path to recovery in the UI.

[ADVISORY] The new client pagination state machine (currentPage, totalPages, showingFirst, showingLast, and the next/previous actions) has no test anywhere in the diff. The totalPages off-by-one shipped precisely through this gap; any future change to the limit default (50), the clamps, or the computed-property deps regresses the admin group page invisibly, since no spec exercises the boundary conditions (user_count == limit multiples, user_count == 0).

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so a 50-member group reports totalPages=2 and showingLast stays false on the real last page. An admin on any group whose member count is a multiple of the 50-item page size (including a plain 50-member group) can click Next into a page that renders zero members as '2/2'; the next-action clamp (line 33) then permits offset=user_count, fetching an empty list, and the phantom page is reachable from every such group with no data-loss recovery needed.

[BUG] The members action now caps every group at 50 rows (default limit 50) while the diff adds pagination controls only to the admin template, so the public group members page — which previously rendered the complete member list for non-automatic groups — silently truncates any group larger than 50 members. Any forum user opening a group's public members page for a 51+ member group sees only the first 50 with no pager to reach the rest; the removed code's own comment ("We should fix the root cause of the bug where if there are more than 200 groups it will truncate") treated truncation as a bug, and this diff makes truncation universal at 50.

[ADVISORY] update silently drops the previous payload contract (params[:group][...], PATCH params[:changes]) while PATCH /admin/groups/:id still routes to update and returns success_json, so existing admin-API clients get a 200 no-op in which their membership edits are discarded and group.visible is also forced to false (absent params[:visible] compares nil == "true"). Anyone scripting the old documented-by-specs endpoints (PUT with group[usernames], PATCH with changes[add]/[delete]) receives success while no members change and the group is silently flipped invisible; no deprecation, version note, or error signals the contract change, so out-of-tree automation corrupts group visibility without any failure response.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten members action (limit/offset pagination plus the new {members, meta:{total,limit,offset}} envelope) ships with zero specs — the only test-shaped file in the diff is spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb and no spec for GroupsController is touched, and any pre-existing spec asserting the old bare-array response shape would already be red, proving no coverage exists. A regression in meta.total/limit/offset, the ordering, or the guardian.ensure_can_see! visibility guard breaks both the public members page and the admin pagination display (both consume meta.total to compute pages) with no failing test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The update context retains only the automatic-group case and deletes the old "is able to update group members" spec, so the non-automatic mainline of the new update action (renaming via params[:name], alias_level, and visible persistence — the path every admin Save click exercises) has no assertion anywhere in the diff. A regression in admin group rename/settings persistence (for example the group.name assignment or the visible == "true" coercion) ships with a green suite, because the single remaining update spec only asserts the automatic-group branch.

[ADVISORY] The new member endpoints are never exercised through the router: the automatic-group removal spec sends xhr :put, :remove_member although the route added in config/routes.rb is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" (the working sibling spec uses :delete), and both add_members/remove_member specs inject group_id directly, which controller specs pass to the action without route recognition. The verb and parameter wiring of the brand-new routes is unverified — if the resources block yields the default :id param while the controller calls params.require(:group_id), every real add/remove from the UI raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400, and no test in this diff can detect it.

[ADVISORY] add_members skips every username that does not match a user (split(",") without trimming, User.find_by_username only on exact match) and still renders success_json, while the diff deletes the old specs that pinned exactly this behavior ("succeeds silently when adding non-existent users") and the controller discards the returned promise with no user-facing feedback. An admin who typos a name or pastes 'sam, jeff' (the ' jeff' token never matches) gets a success response and an uncleared input (the in-diff TODO acknowledges the input is not reset), so a partial add looks identical to full success and the missing member is only discoverable by manually re-reading the list.

[ADVISORY] removeMember reloads the member list with the pre-deletion offset (findMembers clamps offset against the stale user_count), so after deleting the only member shown on the last page the model retains offset equal to the new user_count and renders zero rows. An admin on the last page of a 51-member group who removes its single listed member is left viewing a blank '2/2' member list that reads as an empty group; the offset is never re-clamped to a valid page after the count drops, so recovery requires guessing that Previous still works.

[BUG] The public group members route adopts the paginated fetch (Discourse.Group's default limit of 50) while the diff adds no pagination controls to the public members template, so the public page truncates every group's member list to the first 50 users. Any visitor opening a public group's members tab for a group with more than 50 members sees only 50 names with no way to page to the rest — a regression from the previous behavior where non-automatic groups listed all members (and automatic groups listed 200); a 300-member public group silently hides 250 of its members.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), overcounting pages by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so the next arrow stays enabled on the last real page. An admin viewing a 50-member group sees currentPage=1/totalPages=2 with 'next' enabled; clicking it clamps offset to user_count, the server returns an empty member array, and the UI displays an empty '2/2' page — the member list appears to have vanished (same for 100/limit 50 showing an empty '3/3').

[ADVISORY] The members action changes the public GET /groups/:name/members response contract from a bare serialized array to a {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} envelope, and ships with no spec in this diff pinning the new shape or the pagination logic. Any out-of-tree consumer parsing the old array response (mobile client, plugin, ops script doing .map over the body) now gets an object and breaks at release time, and a future rename of meta.total or the limit default simultaneously breaks both the admin group page and the public members page (both consume findMembers) with no failing test to point at the cause.

[ADVISORY] The add-members flow gives the admin no signal of what happened: the input is not cleared (the diff's own 'TODO: should clear the input'), the server silently skips usernames that User.find_by_username cannot resolve (including unstripped fragments like ' bob' from 'alice, bob' because add_members splits on ',' without stripping), and success_json is rendered either way. An admin who types 'alice, bob' instead of picking from autocomplete gets a partial add (bob silently dropped) while the field still shows both names, so the operation looks accepted; the reloaded list shows only the current page so an alphabetically-later new member never appears in view; and clicking the form's primary Save button never applies the typed usernames at all (save no longer serializes them), leaving the admin with no feedback path in any of these cases.

[ADVISORY] The spec rewrite deletes every edge-case membership test (normal-group rename via update, 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', non-member removal, incremental add/delete) and replaces them only with happy-path specs plus the automatic-group guards, so the new endpoints' edge behaviors are unguarded. A future change to Admin::GroupsController#update's flat-param handling or to add_members' find_by_username loop — e.g., breaking rename for normal groups, whose only spec was deleted here — passes CI and ships silently, since nothing pins update's positive-path behavior or the new endpoints' handling of unknown users/non-members.

[ADVISORY] update switches from the nested group[...] payload to flat params and unconditionally assigns group.visible = (params[:visible] == "true"), so any caller still sending the payload shape this endpoint accepted before this diff gets a silent no-op that also flips the group's visibility off. An existing admin-API script or API-key client that PUTs group: {alias_level: '3', visible: 'true'} receives success_json while its alias_level change is discarded and the group's visible flag is silently set to false — the group disappears from the public groups list with no error returned.

[ADVISORY] remove_member mutates membership through the raw association (group.users.delete(user_id)) while its sibling add_members routes through the model API Group#add, even though the code this same PR removes used group.remove(user) for deletion. The next change that adds bookkeeping to Group#remove (counter maintenance, user/flair cache invalidation) is applied to the model method but silently skipped by remove_member's direct association delete, so removals leave stale state; maintainers of this controller must remember to update two divergent mutation paths.

[BUG] The new `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are member routes inside `resources :groups`, so the path segment binds to `params[:id]` (the same param the sibling `update`/`destroy` actions read via `Group.find(params[:id].to_i)`), while `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member` call `params.require(:group_id)` — a parameter no real request ever carries. Every production PUT/DELETE to /admin/groups/:id/members (the calls the new admin UI's addMembers/removeMember fire) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400, so the rewritten member add/remove feature is entirely non-functional — and the old PATCH and `group[usernames]` paths that could manage members were deleted in this same diff, leaving no working path at all; the new controller specs inject `group_id:` directly via `xhr` and bypass routing, so CI stays green while prod is red.

[BUG] The next action clamps offset to user_count (`Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`), which is a legal but always-empty window, and totalPages (`Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, lines 11-14) overcounts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. For any group with exactly 50/100/150... members, clicking next navigates to a blank member list labeled '3/3' (server returns zero rows for offset == total); the same stranding happens after removeMember deletes the last member of the last page (count 51→50 leaves the admin on an empty '2/2' page), recoverable only by clicking previous.

[BUG] The public group-members route now renders from `model.findMembers()`, which loads only the first 50 members (Discourse.Group's default `limit: 50`), and no pagination control was added anywhere in discourse/templates/group/members.hbs — the pager added by this PR exists only in the admin template. The user-facing members page silently truncates every group to 50 names with no way to see the rest, regressing from the pre-diff endpoint that returned all members (200 for automatic groups); members 51+ of a large public group become invisible to every user including staff.

[ADVISORY] GET /groups/:name/members changes its wire contract with no versioning: the response goes from a bare JSON array to `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`, and the default limit drops from 200 (automatic groups) / unbounded (regular groups) to 50. Out-of-tree consumers — plugins or API scripts that parse the old top-level array with `response.map(...)` — break at runtime, and consumers relying on the full member list silently receive only the first 50 rows.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten update unconditionally assigns `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` and reads only flat params, so legacy nested `group: {...}` payloads are never read and an omitted `visible` evaluates to false. Admin-API scripts doing partial updates (e.g. PUT with only alias_level) silently flip their groups to hidden while receiving success_json, and pre-existing nested-payload callers get a silent no-op success in which nothing they sent was applied; a JSON client sending boolean `true` instead of the string "true" also gets visible=false stored.

[ADVISORY] create persists only `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` while the client's asJSON explicitly sends `alias_level` in the same POST payload, so the field is dropped on creation. An admin who picks a non-default alias_level when creating a group keeps seeing the chosen value in the form while the server persisted 0 (nobody), so the group's mention permissions silently differ from what the UI displays until a later manual save and reload.

[ADVISORY] remove_member removes users via the raw association `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the existing domain method `Group#remove(user)` that the removed PATCH path used, creating two parallel removal implementations for the same operation. Any cleanup logic living in (or later added to) Group#remove or GroupUser destroy callbacks is bypassed by the admin endpoint — the has_many :through association delete also skips join-record destroy callbacks that destroy_all would fire, and the two paths drift the next time Group#remove gains logic.

[ADVISORY] add_members resolves each username via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` and silently skips non-matching names, then returns success_json regardless of how many adds actually happened. An admin who submits 'bob,alice' where alice is a typo or a renamed account gets a success response and a reloaded list showing only bob — the partial failure is indistinguishable from success, with no error, count, or per-name feedback.

[ADVISORY] add_members performs no existing-membership check before `group.add(user)`, replacing the old idempotent full-list `usernames=` update with an unchecked incremental insert on the group_users join table. Re-adding a current member — easy in the new UI where the paginated list hides members not on the visible page and the add box is free-form — silently inserts a duplicate group_users row (this schema has no unique constraint on (group_id, user_id)), so the member appears twice in the list and inflates user_count/meta.total.

[ADVISORY] `{{#unless automatic}}` in the group-member item view template resolves `automatic` against the item view's context — the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property — instead of the group the surrounding group.hbs template binds. The remove control renders on every member row of automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*), where the server forbids removal — clicking it shows a bootbox confirm and then always fails with an error response, presenting an action the system cannot perform.

[ADVISORY] `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` accept arbitrary public input with no clamping and flow straight into `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` on the public members endpoint. Any logged-in user can pass `?limit=-1` (or a negative offset) and PostgreSQL rejects the query with 'LIMIT must not be negative', turning the public endpoint into a 500; a huge limit also re-opens the unbounded member materialization this PR was meant to close.

[BUG] Admin::GroupsController#update silently accepts the previously shipped, spec-tested request payloads — PUT with `group: {name, alias_level, visible, usernames}` and PATCH with `changes: {add, delete}` — returning success_json while discarding all membership edits and renames and unconditionally resetting visible to false whenever top-level params[:visible] is absent. Any client still speaking the old contract (an admin with the group page open across the deploy, a plugin, or an API script built on the deleted specs) saves a group and receives 200 success while the rename and membership changes are dropped and the group's visible flag is flipped to false because `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` evaluates nil == "true" — the edits are lost with no error surfaced anywhere.

[BUG] The rewritten public members action applies a default limit of 50 to every group — the removed code returned the complete member list for non-automatic groups and capped only automatic groups at 200 — while nothing in this diff adds pagination to the public group members page (the group-members route calls findMembers() once with offset 0 and group/members.hbs has no pager). Users viewing /groups/:name/members for a group with more than 50 members see a silently truncated list with no way to reach the remaining members, and automatic groups regress from 200 visible members to 50; the diff institutionalizes at a worse threshold the exact truncation the deleted TODO comment ('We should fix the root cause of the bug where if there are more than 200 groups it will truncate') documents as a bug to fix.

[ADVISORY] The public /groups/:group_id/members response changes from a bare serialized array of members to an object keyed by members/meta, breaking the endpoint's established response contract with no deprecation or compatibility path. Out-of-tree consumers — plugins, themes, and external API integrations that iterate the array — fail on deploy when they receive an object, and any browser still running the pre-deploy JavaScript throws TypeError on result.map inside the old findMembers handler because the promise now resolves to the new envelope, leaving the public members page blank until assets reload.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), so the computed page count is one too high whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. For a group with exactly 100 members at limit 50 the admin page shows 1/3, showingLast is false on the real last page (currentPage 2 vs totalPages 3) so the next arrow stays enabled, and clicking it clamps offset to user_count=100, fetches zero members, and lands the admin on an empty '3/3' page that presents as if all members vanished.

[ADVISORY] create abandons the accepted `group: {name, usernames, visible}` request envelope that the deleted specs asserted — it reads only flat params[:name]/params[:visible] and handles no usernames at all, so one-call group creation with initial members no longer exists. Existing API scripts and plugins that POST the old envelope receive a 422 validation error (params[:name] is nil because the payload nests name under :group, so the stripped name is blank) instead of a created group, and API consumers have no replacement for atomic create-with-members since the new admin UI requires create-then-add as two separate calls.

[ADVISORY] remove_member bypasses the Group#remove model method that the update_patch code this same diff deletes used, instead performing a raw `group.users.delete(user_id)` which loads the group's entire membership association to delete one join row, while the symmetric add_members path goes through the model-level group.add. Whatever Group#remove encapsulates is skipped on the admin removal path, so a contributor who changes membership semantics in Group#add/#remove fixes add_members while remove_member silently diverges, and each removal click on a large manual group materializes every member User object before deleting a single row.

[ADVISORY] The new automatic-group guard spec invokes remove_member with `xhr :put` even though the route this diff wires is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members and the sibling test for the same action six lines below correctly uses `xhr :delete`. A developer replaying the spec's documented request against a real server sends PUT /admin/groups/1/members, which routes to add_members and fails params.require(:usernames) with a 400 instead of the asserted 422, and the suite never exercises the DELETE route added in config/routes.rb so a routing regression keeps every remove_member test green.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff exercises the rewritten public members action — the limit/offset parameter handling, the total count query, and the members/meta envelope — because the only spec changes target Admin::GroupsController. A regression in meta.total, meta.limit, or the 50-member default breaks both the public group members page and the admin pagination math (currentPage/totalPages consume result.meta directly in findMembers) with a green CI suite.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the old update specs that asserted name and membership changes and replaces them with only the automatic-group rename case, leaving the rewritten update action's happy path — persisting name, alias_level, and visible for a non-automatic group — untested. A regression in the primary admin save path, such as breaking the flat params[:alias_level]/params[:visible]/params[:name] assignments this diff introduces, ships with a green suite and silently breaks every admin group edit.

[BUG] create never assigns alias_level from params even though the admin UI's asJSON sends alias_level on the create request, so every newly created group is saved with alias_level 0 regardless of the admin's selection. An admin who picks e.g. 'everyone' (99) on the new-group form gets a group stored as 0 ('nobody'); the Ember model keeps displaying 99 while the DB holds 0, so the group's mention/PM permissions silently differ from what the admin configured until someone re-saves.

[ADVISORY] update changed its request contract from the nested group[name]/group[alias_level]/group[visible] params (and the PATCH changes:{add/delete} membership API) to flat name/alias_level/visible params while keeping the same endpoint path and success_json response, so old-shape requests now return 200 success while applying nothing. Out-of-tree admin-API automation (or a client with a cached pre-deploy JS bundle) that PUTs group:{...} or PATCHes changes:{add:...} gets success_json while the name is ignored, memberships are unchanged, and group.visible is actively forced to false (params[:visible] is nil so '== "true"' is false); group state silently diverges with no error signal to the caller.

[BUG] add_members calls usernames.split(",") on params.require(:usernames) without any type check, so a request carrying usernames as an array (JSON body {"usernames":["a","b"]} or form field usernames[]=a) raises NoMethodError (undefined method 'split' for Array) and returns a 500. Any consumer of this .json admin API endpoint that naturally passes the usernames as an array gets a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 2xx/4xx; the admin UI (comma-joined string) never triggers it, so the defect stays hidden until an API client appears.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and the next action (lines 29-38) clamps offset up to user_count, so paging lands on an empty phantom page. For a group with 100 members at limit 50, the admin sees '1/3', and clicking next from the real last page fetches OFFSET 100 LIMIT 50 (zero rows) and renders a blank list labeled '3/3' with the next link disabled — the admin cannot tell whether members were lost.

[BUG] The remove-link guard {{#unless automatic}} is evaluated inside the per-member item view (the sibling bindings {{member.username}}/{{avatar member}} show the context is the member), so 'automatic' resolves against the Discourse.User object — which has no 'automatic' property — instead of the group, and the remove link renders unconditionally. Admins viewing an automatic group (admins/staff/moderators/trust_level_N) see a working-looking remove icon on every member row; confirming the bootbox prompt sends DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json which the server rejects with 422, and the unhandled promise rejection surfaces no feedback, so removal appears to silently do nothing.

[BUG] remove_member replaces the model's removal path (the deleted update_patch used group.remove(user)) with group.users.delete(user_id), which deletes the group_users join rows via a callback-free delete on the has_many :through association, so any bookkeeping the model performs on membership removal (user_count maintenance, GroupUser destroy callbacks) never runs. After every member removal the group's persisted user_count stays inflated (and destroy-callback cleanup is skipped), so the public groups list and the admin pagination show too many members and phantom pages until the count is recomputed; the removal spec only asserts group.users.count == 0 so it cannot catch this.

[ADVISORY] members passes user-controlled (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and params[:offset].to_i straight into .limit/.offset with no bounds validation, and this diff newly applies user-controlled pagination to every group rather than only automatic ones. Any user who can see a group can hit GET /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 (or limit=-1) and get a Postgres 'OFFSET must not be negative' 500 on the public endpoint (error-log noise and cheap error-tracking spam), and an arbitrarily large limit serializes the entire membership of huge groups in a single response.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten GroupsController#members — pagination plus the new {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} response envelope consumed by both the public group members page and the admin member list (group.js findMembers reads result.meta) — has no controller spec anywhere in this diff, and any pre-existing members spec would necessarily have been updated for the new envelope. A regression in limit/offset/meta handling (wrong total, offset echo, envelope shape) ships silently: both the public members page and the admin group member list render blank or wrongly with no failing spec to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten Admin::GroupsController#update's non-automatic path — persisting the new flat param contract `params[:name]`/`params[:alias_level]`/`params[:visible]` (groups_controller.rb lines 37-40) — is covered by no test: the diff deletes `it "is able to update group members"` (the only spec that asserted a normal group's rename persisted, `group.name.should == 'fred'`) and the surviving `.update` spec in this, the diff's only test file (checked: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb is the sole spec changed; its .index/.create/.update/.destroy/.refresh_automatic_groups/.add_members/.remove_member contexts contain no non-automatic update test), exercises only the automatic-group branch, so the restructured param shape and the alias_level assignment (asserted nowhere in the entire suite) are unverified. A dropped or misnamed parameter in update (e.g. `params[:alias_lvl]`) ships with a fully green suite; admins editing a regular group via the admin UI's Save button — which PUTs exactly these flat params through Group#asJSON — receive `success_json` on an untouched record, so name/alias_level/visibility edits silently fail to persist while the UI reports success.

[BUG] add_members passes each token of the raw comma-joined string to `User.find_by_username(username)` without stripping (`usernames.split(",").each do |username| if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), so a padded token like `" alice"` from an admin typing "bob, alice" in the free-text Add-members field matches no user and is silently skipped, and the only parsing spec — `usernames: [user1.username, user2.username].join(",")` (spec line 104), the no-space all-valid happy path — never exercises the tokenizing edge, so the drop ships unverified (the old suite's pins for unknown-user skips, e.g. "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users", were deleted with the PATCH tests rather than ported). An admin who types "bob, alice" into the new admin group Add members input gets a 200 success_json, the member list reloads without alice, and no error surfaces anywhere; CI stays green because no spec posts a spaced or unknown username to add_members.

[ADVISORY] The automatic-group guard spec drives remove_member with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` even though routes.rb wires that action only under `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (its sibling test three lines below correctly uses `xhr :delete`), and because rspec-rails controller specs dispatch by action name without consulting routes.rb, the suite validates the action through a request shape production can never make. Any routing regression on the new member endpoints — a flipped verb, renamed action, or dropped route in config/routes.rb — passes the entire suite while the admin UI's real `type: "DELETE"`/`type: "PUT"` calls to /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json (group.js removeMember/addMembers) start returning 404/500 in production; the in-diff :put/:delete inconsistency shows these specs no longer mirror the HTTP contract they claim to verify.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create reads flat params[:name]/params[:visible] while the previously shipped client and existing admin-API scripts post the nested group[name]/group[visible] contract, so their valid payloads arrive with name nil. An admin with a stale pre-deploy bundle (or any existing automation creating groups via the admin API) submitting a group with a name gets a 422 'Name can't be blank' style validation error even though a name was supplied — group creation is broken until the client reloads the new assets or the script is rewritten to the flat format.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` was changed to read flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`) instead of the prior nested contract (`params[:group][:name]`, `params[:group][:visible]`) that the old client code used (see removed `createWithUsernames`/`asJSON` which previously sent `{ group: { ... } }`). The new JS model now posts flat `data: this.asJSON()` (no `group` wrapper), so it works after asset refresh, but any pre-deploy/stale client bundle or existing automation still posting `group[name]` will result in `group.name` becoming `''` and `group.save` failing, returning `render_json_error` (422). This regression is verifiable from the controller and client changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members splits the usernames param on ',' with no whitespace normalization while User.find_by_username exact-matches username_lower without stripping, so space-padded entries match no user. An admin who types or pastes 'user1, user2' (space after the comma) into the selector and hits Add gets success_json and a reloaded list containing only user1 — user2 is silently not enrolled in the group (losing whatever post/category access that membership grants) with no error to indicate the miss.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` with no `strip`/whitespace normalization. If the client sends a string like `"user1, user2"`, the second token will be `" user2"` and will not match a normal username lookup, so that user will not be added. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, making the failure silent. This behavior is directly implied by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members reads `params.require(:group_id)`, but the route added for it (config/routes.rb:49-50, a bare `put 'members'` inside the admin `resources :groups` block) is a member route that supplies the group key as `params[:id]`, so every real request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400. Every 'add members' click in the admin UI sends PUT /admin/groups/:id/members.json and receives a 400; no member is ever added through the shipped UI, the rejected promise has no handler anywhere on the path (model addMembers, controller action), so the admin gets zero feedback and the feature is dead on arrival — the controller specs pass only because `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: ...` bypasses routing entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/routes.rb`, `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` are defined inside `resources :groups` without `collection`, so they are member routes and will be invoked as `/admin/groups/:id/members(.json)` (the UI does exactly this: `'/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`). Member routes supply the group identifier as `params[:id]`, but both controller actions require `:group_id` (`Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`), which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` at runtime. The specs pass because they call the controller actions directly with `group_id:` and thus don’t exercise routing/param naming.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] remove_member reads `params.require(:group_id)` while its route (config/routes.rb:49, bare `delete 'members'` inside the admin `resources :groups` block) supplies the group key as `params[:id]`, so every real removal request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400. The admin confirms the bootbox dialog, the DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json returns 400, the member is never removed, and the unhandled rejection means nothing is shown — the remove link appears to do nothing for every non-automatic group, undetectable by the controller specs which pass `group_id:` directly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s route is defined *inside* `namespace :admin` → `resources :groups do ... delete "members" ... end`, which in Rails generates a member-scoped route of the form `/admin/groups/:group_id/members(.:format)` (i.e., it supplies `params[:group_id]`, not `params[:id]`). The AJAX URL `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` will populate that segment into `params[:group_id]` regardless of the segment name in the path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members silently discards every username that does not resolve (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)` skips the nil case) and still returns success_json. An admin who submits 'alice,typo' gets a success response and a reloaded member list that simply lacks the typo'd user — the membership is dropped with no error, no log, and no UI signal (the input is not even cleared, per the TODO), so permission-granting additions fail invisibly.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the loop `usernames.split(",").each` only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, and does nothing for unknown usernames. Regardless, it then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds (which it will even if zero users were added), so the API/UI can report success while silently skipping typo’d/nonexistent usernames with no error or feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members calls `group.add(user)` with no existing-membership check before pushing into the users association. Re-adding a user who is already a member — the natural case, since addMembers never clears the input and has no in-flight guard against double-clicks — raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the join-table insert and returns a 500, with usernames earlier in the comma list already inserted, leaving partially-applied membership and no indication to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff loops `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each matched user with no guard against already-existing membership (`group.add(user)` is unconditional) and no transaction/rescue around the loop. Since `addMembers` in the controller/template does not clear the input (explicit TODO) and has no in-flight/double-click protection, it can resend the same usernames, and a duplicate join-table insert can raise (e.g., `RecordNotUnique`) and return a 500 mid-loop, potentially leaving earlier inserts applied and later ones not attempted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update switched the wire format from the old `{group: {...}}` envelope to flat params with no compatibility handling, so a client still sending the envelope yields nil for every flat param read and `params[:visible] == 'true'` therefore assigns false. An admin whose tab still runs the pre-deploy bundle (or any API consumer of the documented admin groups API) saves a group, gets success_json, and the group is silently flipped to hidden (visible=false) with its name/alias_level/membership edits dropped — the UI reports success while the group's visibility is corrupted; the reverse skew (new flat client vs an old server) raises NoMethodError on the nil envelope and 500s.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the server-side Admin::GroupsController wire format from nested `params[:group]` (old `update_put`/`create` reading `params[:group][:...]`) to flat params (`params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:name]`) with no backward-compat handling. In `update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to `false` when an older client sends only `group[visible]`, silently flipping visibility while returning `success_json`. Similarly, name/alias_level won’t apply because the flat keys are absent. The reverse skew is also supported by the diff: the old code used `payload = params[:group]` and dereferenced it, which would raise if a newer client sends flat params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public members endpoint applies `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` straight to the query with `.to_i` and no bounds — no upper cap and no clamp against negative values. GET /groups/<name>/members?limit=-1 builds `LIMIT -1` and PostgreSQL rejects it, returning a 500 where the API contract wants a bounded 4xx; and ?limit=99999999 serializes a large group's entire membership (hundreds of thousands of rows for trust-level automatic groups) in one unbounded response on a public endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces unbounded, unclamped pagination params: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then applies them directly to the query via `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no upper cap on `limit` and no clamping of negative values. This makes `?limit=-1`/`?offset=-1` possible; Rails will pass these through to SQL (`LIMIT -1` / `OFFSET -1`), which can raise DB errors (500). Similarly, very large `limit` values can force huge public responses, since this endpoint is under `GroupsController` (not admin) and now paginates all groups’ members, not just automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] removeMember and addMembers invoke `self.findMembers()` inside their `.then` without returning it and with no rejection handler, while the controller actions (admin-group.js.es6:56, 64) drop the returned promises entirely. The outer promise resolves success before the member list reload even starts, and when any link in the chain fails (a 4xx on add/remove, an expired session, a failed reload) the rejection is swallowed with no handler anywhere — the admin receives zero feedback and the member list silently shows stale state.

[BUG] next/previous commit `group.set('offset', offset)` before findMembers resolves, with no rollback on failure, no in-flight guard, and the returned promise discarded by the {{action}} helper so its rejection is unhandled. Clicking next during a failed or slow request leaves the page indicator advanced (currentPage recomputes off the committed offset) while the member list still shows the old page — desynced until another navigation succeeds; rapid clicks issue overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses overwrite members/offset (last response wins), settling the list on a page the admin did not select.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that findMembers is async, its returned promise is discarded/unhandled (possible unhandled rejection), and that state (offset/page indicator) updates before the async call resolves, causing desynchronization and race conditions with overlapping/out-of-order responses. This matches the golden issue about unhandled async findMembers leading to a race where member data isn’t immediately available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is a positive multiple of limit. A group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 displays totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist; showingLast is false at the real last page, so the admin clicks next, offset is clamped to 100, the server returns an empty member array, and the page renders '3/3' with zero members — the admin is shown an apparently empty group.

adjudication.rationale: `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3). With `showingLast` defined as `currentPage == totalPages`, the UI will not consider the real last page as last. Clicking `next` sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` (so it can become exactly `user_count`), and `Group.findMembers()` sends that `offset` to `/groups/:name/members.json`; in `GroupsController#members` the query `limit(limit).offset(offset)` will then return an empty set when `offset == total`, producing an empty member list on a bogus final page.

Every client running the previous bundle during the rolling deploy (open tabs) executes `result.map(...)` on the new object and throws TypeError, breaking the group members page for those users; the new client against an old server is the mirror image (`result.meta.total` on an array), leaving the member list silently empty with the rejection unhandled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (an object). The old client code (shown removed in `discourse/models/group.js`) did `result.map(...)` on the AJAX response, which would throw if the server now returns an object. The new client code now expects `result.meta.total` and `result.members`, which would fail against an older server still returning an array.
